content:
We need to find a template that when applied to the given molecule (target) reproduces the forward carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). The given molecule is a substrate? Actually initial_molecule is the product? The description: "when applied to the molecule below reproduces the reaction: In a carbonyl-ene reaction, an alkene reacts with an allylic hydrogen and a carbonyl group to form a new carbon-carbon bond... The result of the reaction is the formation of a new carbon-carbon bond and a new stereocenter at the site of the allylic hydrogen, in which one of the substituents is going to be a hydroxyl group. Additionally, the reaction involves the change in the order of a C=C bond to a C-C bond, and a C=O bond to a C-O bond. 'ketones' and 'C-C double bonds' are gone, while a 'aliphatic hydroxyl' and a 'five-membered rings' are formed."

Thus the forward reaction: starting material has alkene and carbonyl (ketone) and after reaction you get hydroxyl and five-membered ring (intramolecular). The given initial_molecule likely is the product (has hydroxyl, five-membered ring). Indeed the SMILES: [CH2]=[C] attached to aromatic ring and a cyclobutane? Let's decode: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... ) ... [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])... So there is a five-membered ring (C9-10-11-12-13) with OH on C13. So product has hydroxyl and five-membered ring. So we need retrosynthetic step: break to precursor with alkene and ketone. So we need to find a template that does carbonyl-ene retro (i.e., reverse of forward). The template likely is something like "C=O + C=C -> C-O + C-C". We need to search for templates that break C=O and C=C and form C-O and C-C. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["C-C double bonds","ketones"] and functional_groups_formed = ["aliphatic hydroxyls","five-membered rings"] maybe. Let's see available functional groups list. Use get_available_functional_groups.
